body:
WHAT
When the user clicks "Always allow" on an ordinary command prompt, the engine remembers the command's shape, not its exact text: `mkdir -p a/b` grants all `mkdir`; for multi-command CLIs like git or npm it keeps two tokens (`git push`); for `npm/pnpm/yarn run <script>` it keeps three (`npm run build`). Compound or substituted commands (pipes, `;`, `$(…)`, quotes) stay literal. The prompt payload shows the derived grant so the user sees the scope.

WHY
Without it every slightly different argument list re-asks and 'always allow' reads as broken; without the literal fallback a grant for `git push` could silently cover `git push --force`, which is why deletion-guard approvals never go through shape derivation.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/permissions.ts — deriveAlwaysGrant(), MULTI_COMMAND_CLIS, ExactGrant.prefix, PermissionEngine.check() 'ask' branch (computes `shape` when tool.permissionClass === 'execute', passes `grant` in PermissionRequestPayload, calls grantExact(tool, shape, true) on allow_always), PermissionEngine.matchesExact() (prefix match on `subject + ' '`), PermissionEngine.grantExact(), persistExact callback. engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session constructor's persistExact lambda pushes into settings.permissions.allowExact and calls addExactPermission().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. deriveAlwaysGrant('mkdir -p a/b') returns 'mkdir'; deriveAlwaysGrant('git push origin main') returns 'git push'; deriveAlwaysGrant('npm run build --silent') returns 'npm run build'.
2. deriveAlwaysGrant returns undefined for 'ls | grep x', 'a && b', 'echo $(date)', 'rm "my file"', and for 'git --version' (subcommand starts with '-').
3. After an allow_always answer on an out-of-workspace-forced 'ask' for an execute tool with subject 'mkdir -p a', the persistExact callback is called with ('Bash','mkdir',true) and a later check with subject 'mkdir -p b' resolves allowed:true, source:'rule' without calling requestApproval.
4. The PermissionRequestPayload passed to requestApproval carries grant:'git push' for subject 'git push origin main' and omits `grant` when the shape equals the subject (e.g. 'mkdir').
5. A prefix grant {tool:'Bash', subject:'git push', prefix:true} does NOT satisfy the deletion guard: a later `git push --force` call still calls requestApproval with source 'deletion-guard' (matchesExact with literalOnly ignores prefix grants).
